<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.1pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<div class="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div class="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman;">18</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">
<div class="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><i>Patents &#8212; </i>Patents&nbsp;are amortized on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives or agreement terms.&nbsp; As of December&nbsp;31, 2020, the Company's patents had a remaining estimated weighted average useful life of 8.5 years.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><i>Impairment of Long-lived Assets &#8212; </i>The Company reviews its long-lived assets, including property, plant and equipment and patents, for impairment when indicators of impairment are present and the undiscounted cash flows estimated to be generated by those assets are less than the assets&#8217; carrying amount. Any impairment loss recorded is measured as the amount by which the carrying value of the assets exceeds the fair value of the assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;To date, the Company has determined that no&nbsp;loss on impairment of long-lived assets exists.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><i>Fair Value of Financial Instruments</i> &#8212; The carrying amounts of financial instruments, including cash and cash equivalents, short-term investments, trade receivables, accounts payable, and accrued liabilities approximate fair value due to the short maturities of these instruments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The fair value of long-term debt approximates its carrying value and has been estimated based on interest rates being offered for similar debt having the same or similar remaining maturities and collateral requirements.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.1pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;"><i>Revenue recognition</i>.&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue is measured based on consideration specified in the contract with a customer, adjusted for any applicable estimates of variable consideration and other factors affecting the transaction price, including noncash consideration, consideration paid or payable to customers and significant financing components.&nbsp; While most of the Company&#8217;s revenue is contracted with customers through one-time purchase orders and short-term contracts, the Company does have long-term arrangements with certain customers.&nbsp; Revenue from all customers is recognized when a performance obligation is satisfied by transferring control of a distinct good or service to a customer.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">Individually promised goods and services in a contract are considered a distinct performance obligation and accounted for separately if the customer can benefit from the individual good or service on its own or with other resources that are readily available to the customer and the good or service is separately identifiable from other promises in the arrangement.&nbsp;&nbsp;When an arrangement includes multiple performance obligations, the consideration is allocated between the performance obligations in proportion to their estimated standalone selling price.&nbsp;&nbsp;Costs related to products delivered are recognized in the period incurred, unless criteria for capitalization of costs are met. Costs of revenues consist primarily of direct labor, manufacturing overhead, materials and components.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not incur significant upfront costs to obtain a contract.&nbsp;&nbsp;If costs to obtain a contract were to become material, the costs would be recorded as an asset and amortized to expense in a manner consistent with the related recognition of revenue.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">The Company excludes from revenue governmental assessed and imposed taxes on revenue transactions that are invoiced to customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company includes freight billed to customers in revenue. Shipping and handling costs associated with outbound freight after control over a product has transferred to a customer are accounted for as a fulfillment cost and are included in cost of goods sold.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">The timing of revenue recognition, billings and cash collections results in accounts receivable on the balance sheet.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;"><i>Performance obligations</i>.&nbsp;&nbsp;A performance obligation is a promise in a contract to transfer a distinct good or service to the customer.&nbsp;&nbsp;A contract&#8217;s transaction price is allocated to each distinct performance obligation in proportion to its standalone selling price and recognized as revenue when, or as, the performance obligation is satisfied.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#8217;s various performance obligations and the timing or method of revenue recognition are discussed below:&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">The Company sells its products to both distributors and end-users. Each unit of product delivered under a customer order represents a distinct and separate performance obligation as the customer can benefit from each unit on its own or with other resources that are readily available to the customer and each unit of product is separately identifiable from other products in the arrangement.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">The transaction price for the Company&#8217;s products is the invoiced amount.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not have variable consideration in the form of refunds, credits, rebates, price concessions, pricing incentives or other items impacting transaction price.&nbsp;&nbsp;The purchase order pricing in arrangements with customers is deemed to approximate standalone selling price; therefore, the Company does not need to allocate proceeds on a relative standalone selling price allocation between performance obligations.&nbsp; The Company&nbsp;does not disclose information about remaining performance obligations that have original expected durations of one year or less. There are no material obligations that extend beyond one year.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">Revenue is recognized when transfer of control occurs as defined by the terms in the customer agreement. The Company immediately recognizes incidental items that are immaterial in the context of the contract.&nbsp; The Company does not have any significant financing components in its customer arrangements as payment is received at or shortly after the point of sale, generally thirty to ninety days.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">The Company estimates returns based on an analysis of historical experience if the right to return products is granted to its customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not record a return asset as non-conforming products are generally not returned.&nbsp; The Company&#8217;s return policy does not vary by geography.&nbsp;&nbsp;The customer has no rotation or price protection rights.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:#ff0000;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<div class="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">
<div class="PGNUM" style="text-align: center; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman;">19</div>

<hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000">
<div class="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;"><i>Trade receivables.</i> &nbsp;Trade receivables include amounts invoiced and currently due from customers and are </font>financial instruments that also expose the Company to concentration of credit risk.&nbsp; The large number of customers comprising the Company&#8217;s customer base and their dispersion across different geographic areas limits such exposure.&nbsp;&nbsp;<font style="color:null;">The amounts due are stated at their net estimated realizable value.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company records an allowance for doubtful accounts to provide for the estimated amount of receivables that will not be collected and&nbsp;</font>adequately provide for credit losses.&nbsp; T<font style="color:null;">he allowance is based on a review of all outstanding amounts on an on-going basis. Management determines the allowance for doubtful accounts by regularly evaluating individual customer receivables and considers a customer&#8217;s financial condition, credit history, and current economic conditions. Trade receivables are written off when deemed uncollectible. Recoveries of trade receivables previously written off are recorded when received. Accounts are considered past due if payment is not received according to agreed-upon terms.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>A small percentage of the trade receivables balance is denominated in a foreign currency with no concentration in any given country.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the end of each reporting period, the Company analyzes the receivable balance for customers paying in a foreign currency. These balances are adjusted to each quarter or year-end spot rate.&nbsp; Foreign currency transactions and translation adjustments did not have a significant effect on the Balance Sheets,&nbsp;the Statements of Operations, Stockholders&#8217; Equity or&nbsp;Cash Flows for 2020&nbsp;and 2019.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;"><i>Sales commissions.</i> &nbsp;Sales commissions paid to sales representatives are eligible for capitalization as they are incremental costs that would not have been incurred without entering into a specific sales arrangement and are recoverable through the expected margin on the transaction.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recognizes the incremental costs of obtaining contracts as an expense when incurred, as the amortization period of the assets that would have otherwise been recognized is one year or less.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company records these costs in selling, general, and administrative expense.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;"><i>Product warranties.</i> &nbsp;&nbsp;The Company offers warranties on various products and services. These warranties are assurance type warranties that are not sold on a standalone basis; therefore, they are not considered distinct performance obligations.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company estimates the costs that may be incurred under its warranties and records a liability in the amount of such costs at the time the revenue is recognized for the product sale.&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 26pt; text-align: left;"><font style="color:null;"><i>International revenue.</i> &nbsp; The Company markets its products to numerous countries in North America, Europe, Latin America, Asia and other parts of the world.&nbsp;&nbsp;Foreign sales were approximately 29.7% and 29.4% of total sales in 2020&nbsp;and 2019, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><i>Deferred Taxes</i> &#8212; Deferred taxes are provided on a liability method whereby deferred tax assets are recognized for deductible temporary differences and operating loss and tax credit carryforwards and deferred tax liabilities are recognized for taxable temporary differences.&nbsp;&nbsp;Temporary differences are the differences between the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and their tax basis.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance when, in the opinion of management, it is more likely than not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company classifies deferred tax assets and liabilities as noncurrent.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted for the effects of changes in tax laws and rates on the date of enactment.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">The Company follows the accounting standard on accounting for uncertainty in income taxes, which addresses the determination of whether tax benefits claimed or expected to be claimed on a tax return should be recorded in the financial statements.&nbsp; Under this guidance, the Company may recognize the tax benefit from an uncertain tax position only if it is more likely than not that the tax position will be sustained on examination by taxing authorities, based on the technical merits of the position.&nbsp; The tax benefits recognized in the financial statements from such a position are measured based on the largest benefit that has a greater than 50 percent likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement.&nbsp; The guidance on accounting for uncertainty in income taxes also addresses derecognition, classification, interest and penalties on income taxes, and accounting in interim periods.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><i>Earnings Per Share (EPS) </i>&#8212;<i>&nbsp;</i>Basic EPS is calculated using net income (loss) divided by the weighted average of common shares outstanding.&nbsp;&nbsp;Diluted EPS is similar to Basic EPS except that the weighted average number of common shares outstanding is increased to include the number of additional common shares, when&nbsp;dilutive, that would have been outstanding if the potential dilutive common shares, such as those shares subject to options, had been issued.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.05pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">Shares used in the calculation of diluted EPS are summarized below:</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.1pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">If the Company was in a net income position at December 31, 2020, all 17,500&nbsp;options outstanding with a weighted average exercise price of $6.97&nbsp;would have remained excluded from the computation of weighted average common and common equivalent shares outstanding as the options were anti-dilutive.&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">Restricted stock units of approximately 54,300 shares for the year-end December 31, 2020 would have remained excluded from the computation of weighted average common and common equivalent shares outstanding as they were anti-dilutive due to the amount of weighted-average unrecognized compensation related to these grants.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">At December 31, 2019, options to purchase 19,250 shares of common stock with a weighted average exercise price of $11.32&nbsp;were outstanding, but were excluded from the computation of common share equivalents because they were anti-dilutive.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><i>Employee Stock Plan -</i> The Company accounts for employee stock options under the provision of ASC 718, Compensation &#8212; Stock Compensation.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><i>Recent Accounting Pronouncements -&nbsp;</i>In June 2016, the FASB issued ASU No. 2016-13,&nbsp;Measurement of Credit Losses on Financial Instruments, which revises guidance for the accounting for credit losses on financial instruments within its scope, and in November 2018, issued ASU No. 2018-19 and in April 2019, issued ASU No. 2019-04 and in May 2019, issued ASU No. 2019-05, and in November 2019, issued ASU No. 2019-11, which amended the standard. The new standard introduces an approach, based on expected losses, to estimate credit losses on certain types of financial instruments and modifies the impairment model for available-for-sale debt securities. The new approach to estimating credit losses (referred to as the current expected credit losses model) applies to most financial assets measured at amortized cost and certain other instruments, including trade and other receivables, loans, held-to-maturity debt securities, net investments in leases and off-balance-sheet credit exposures. This ASU is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2022, including interim periods within those fiscal years, with early adoption permitted. Entities are required to apply the standard&#8217;s provisions as a cumulative-effect adjustment to retained earnings as of the beginning of the first reporting period in which the guidance is adopted. The Company is still evaluating the impact of this ASU.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><i>Use of Estimates</i> &#8212; The preparation of the financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Actual results could differ from those estimates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Significant estimates include the allowance for doubtful trade receivables, the reserve for inventory obsolescence, undiscounted cash flows generated from long-live assets&nbsp;and the valuation allowance for deferred tax assets.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.1pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:-28.1pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

			<td id=".amt.2" style="width: 12%; text-align: right; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; border-bottom: 3px double rgb(0, 0, 0);">&#8212;</td>
			<td id=".trail.2" nowrap="true" style="width: 1%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; padding-bottom: 3px;">&nbsp;</td>
			<td id=".lead.3" style="width: 1%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</td>
			<td id=".symb.3" style="width: 1%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; border-bottom: 3px double rgb(0, 0, 0);">$</td>
			<td id=".amt.3" style="width: 12%; text-align: right; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; border-bottom: 3px double rgb(0, 0, 0);">&#8212;</td>
			<td id=".trail.3" nowrap="true" style="width: 1%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin-left: 0pt; padding-bottom: 3px;">&nbsp;</td>
		</tr>

</table>
</div>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 37pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">As of December 31, 2020, the Company has federal net operating loss carry-forwards and research and development credit carryovers of $1,847,000 and $104,000, respectively, and begin expiring in&nbsp;2037. The Company&#8217;s state net operating loss carryforwards and research and development credit carryovers at&nbsp;December 31, 2020&nbsp;total&nbsp;$468,000 and $214,000, respectively, and begin expiring in&nbsp;2026.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">The Company is subject to federal and state taxation. As of&nbsp;December 31, 2020,&nbsp;with few exceptions, the Company is&nbsp;no longer subject to examination prior to tax year&nbsp;2017.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">In accounting for uncertainty in income taxes, we recognize the financial statement benefit of a tax position only after determining that the relevant tax authority would more likely than not sustain the position following an audit. For tax positions meeting the more likely than not threshold, the amount recognized in the financial statements is the largest benefit that has a greater than 50 percent likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement with the relevant tax authority. As of&nbsp;December 31, 2020, the Company does not have any unrecognized tax benefits. The Company recognizes interest and penalties accrued on any unrecognized tax benefits as a component of income tax expense. We do not expect any material changes in our unrecognized tax benefits over the next 12 months.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 18pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">The Company establishes a valuation allowance to reduce the deferred tax assets when it is more likely than not that a deferred tax asset will not be realizable. On the basis of this evaluation, as of&nbsp;December 31, 2020 and 2019,&nbsp;a full valuation allowance has been recorded to reserve for&nbsp;deferred tax assets, which are&nbsp;not&nbsp;expected to be realized.&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<div class="PGBK" style="width: 100%; margin-left: 0pt; margin-right: 0pt">

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">Intangible assets consist of patents, and patent applications.&nbsp;&nbsp;Capitalized patent application costs are included with patents.&nbsp;&nbsp;Intangible assets are amortized on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives or terms of their agreement, whichever is shorter.&nbsp; &nbsp; The Company wrote off costs related to abandoned patent applications of $17,000 in 2020 and $93,000 in 2019.&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.8pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">In connection with a&nbsp;license agreement, the Company has agreed to pay royalties ranging from 3% to 5% on the sales of products subject to the agreement.&nbsp; The Company incurred $8,000 and $10,000 of expense under these agreements during 2020&nbsp;and 2019, respectively, which are included in selling, general and administrative expenses in the Statements of Operations.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.8pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:-27pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="161317" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1582756571993">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;">

		<tr style="vertical-align: top;">
			<td style="width: 27pt;">
			<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">4.</p>
			</td>
			<td>
			<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">RETIREMENT PLAN</p>
			</td>
		</tr>

</table>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.8pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:-28.8pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">The Company has established a salary deferral plan under Section&nbsp;401(k)&nbsp;of the Internal Revenue Code.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such deferrals accumulate on a tax-deferred basis until the employee withdraws the funds.&nbsp; Historically, the Company has contributed&nbsp;up to 5% of each eligible employee&#8217;s compensation.&nbsp; As part of cost&nbsp;reduction efforts in 2020 the Company temporarily suspended its 5% contribution in 2020. Total retirement expense for the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2020&nbsp;and 2019&nbsp;was approximately $120,000 and $241,000, respectively.&nbsp; The Company anticipates it&nbsp;will resume at least a portion of its 5% 401(k) contribution in 2021 as business conditions allow.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
</div>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="161318" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1582756589736">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;">

		<tr style="vertical-align: top;">
			<td style="width: 27pt;">
			<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">5.</p>
			</td>
			<td>
			<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">SEGMENT INFORMATION</p>
			</td>
		</tr>

</table>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.8pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:-28.8pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">The Company&#8217;s reportable segments are strategic business units that offer different products and have varied customer bases.&nbsp;&nbsp;There are four&nbsp;reportable segments:&nbsp; Chromaline, IKONICS Imaging, Digital Texturing (DTX) and Advanced Material Solutions (AMS).&nbsp; Chromaline sells screen printing film, emulsions, and inkjet receptive film primarily to distributors and some end users.&nbsp; IKONICS Imaging sells photo resistant film, art supplies, glass, and related abrasive etching equipment to both end users and distributors.&nbsp; AMS provides sound deadening and weight reduction technology to the aerospace industry along with products and services for etched composites, ceramics, glass and silicon wafers.&nbsp;&nbsp;DTX includes products and customers related to patented and proprietary inkjet technology used for mold texturing and prototyping.&nbsp; The accounting policies of the segments are the same as those described in the summary of significant accounting policies included in Note 1.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">Management evaluates the performance of each segment based on the components of divisional income, and does not allocate assets and liabilities to segments except for trade receivables.&nbsp;&nbsp;Financial information with respect to the reportable segments follows:</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:30pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.1pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>For the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2020:</b></p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="161319" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1582756608874">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;">

		<tr style="vertical-align: top;">
			<td style="width: 27pt;">
			<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">6.</p>
			</td>
			<td>
			<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">STOCKHOLDERS&#8217; EQUITY</p>
			</td>
		</tr>

</table>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.8pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:-28.8pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">The Company maintains the 2019 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2019&nbsp;Plan&#8221;). The 2019&nbsp;Plan replaced the 1995 Incentive Stock Option Plan (the "1995 Plan) upon its ratification by shareholders in April 2019.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The 1995 plan authorized the issuance of up to 442,750 shares of common stock through grants of restricted stock units and options.&nbsp; Of those shares, 5,000 were subject to outstanding options as of December 31, 2020.&nbsp; Awards granted under the 1995&nbsp;Plan will remain in effect until they are exercised or expire according to their terms.&nbsp; &nbsp; At the time the 2019 Plan was approved, there were 102,157 shares reserved for future grants under the 1995 Plan which will no longer be available for future grants.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">Under the terms of the 2019&nbsp;Plan, the number of shares of common stock that may be the subject of awards and issued under the 2019&nbsp;Plan was initially set at 102,157.&nbsp; Subsequent to the approval of the 2019 Plan, 11,750&nbsp;outstanding options granted under the 1995 Plan were forfeited.&nbsp; Under the terms of the 2019 Plan, those forfeited options are added back to the 2019 Plan reserve pool.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2020, 54,300 restricted stock units (RSUs) and 13,250 options have been granted&nbsp;under the 2019&nbsp;Plan, of&nbsp;which 750 stock options have been forfeited, bringing the number of shares of common stock available for future awards under the 2019 Plan to 47,107.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">The Company charged compensation expense of $22,000&nbsp;and $9,000&nbsp;against the loss in 2020&nbsp;and 2019, respectively.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">As of December&nbsp;31, 2020, there was approximately $348,000 of unrecognized compensation expense related to unvested share-based compensation awards granted which is expected to be recognized over the next three years.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">No stock options were exercised in 2020&nbsp;or 2019</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">The fair value of options granted was estimated using the Black-Scholes option pricing model with the following assumptions:</p>

<div class="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">&nbsp;</div>
</div>

<p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">There were 54,300 RSUs granted in 2020.&nbsp; The shares underlying the awards were assigned a weighted average value of $6.11 per share, which was the closing price of the Company's common stock on the date of grants.&nbsp; These awards are scheduled to vest over three years.&nbsp; No RSUs were granted in 2019 to employees.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">RSU activity during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2020 is summarized as follows:</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">In 2017, the Company&#8217;s board of directors had authorized the repurchase of 100,000 shares of common stock.&nbsp;&nbsp; A total of 33,500&nbsp;shares have been repurchased under this program in prior years.&nbsp; On April 29, 2019 the Company's board of directors approved an additional repurchase authorization of 33,500 shares of the&nbsp;Company's common stock bringing the total repurchase authorization to 100,000 shares of common stock.&nbsp; A total of 40,699&nbsp;shares have been repurchased under this program including the 7,199&nbsp;shares repurchased during 2019.&nbsp; &nbsp;As of December 31, 2020, 92,801 shares were authorized to be repurchased under the plan.&nbsp; The share&nbsp;repurchase&nbsp;authorizations do&nbsp;not have an expiration date and there were no repurchases of common stock in 2020.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-size: 1pt; margin: 0; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

			<td>
			<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">LONG-TERM DEBT</p>
			</td>
		</tr>

</table>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.8pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:-28.8pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><b>Duluth Economic Development Authority Loan</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">On April&nbsp;1, 2016,&nbsp;the Company entered into a financing agreement (the &#8220;Financing Agreement&#8221;) under which the Duluth Economic Development Authority (the &#8220;Issuer&#8221;) agreed to sell $3,415,000 of its Tax Exempt Industrial Revenue Bonds, Series&nbsp;2016 (IKONICS Project) (the &#8220;Bonds&#8221;) to Wells Fargo Bank, National Association (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;), and the Bank agreed to lend to the Company the proceeds received from the sale of the Bonds (the &#8220;Loan&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The closing of the sale of the Bonds occurred on April&nbsp;29, 2016. The proceeds from the Loan were used to finance the construction of&nbsp;a 27,300-square foot building as well as related equipment for use in the Company&#8217;s manufacture of sound deadening technology used in the aerospace industry and products consisting of etched composites, ceramics, glass and silicon wafers, to be located in Duluth, Minnesota (the &#8220;Project&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Loan requires monthly payments of approximately $18,000, including interest. The Loan bears interest at a rate of 2.60% per year, subject to change based upon changes to the maximum federal corporate tax rate.&nbsp; Including debt costs of approximately $139,000, the Loan&#8217;s effective interest rate was 3.23% at December 31, 2020.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">The Company is subject to certain customary covenants set forth in the associated covenant agreement, including a requirement that the Company maintain a debt service coverage ratio of not less than 1.25 to 1.00.&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">The Loan is subject to mandatory purchase provisions, under which any owners of the Bonds (the &#8220;Owners&#8221;) may tender the Bonds to the Issuer on April 1, 2021, which would result in the Company repaying the outstanding loan principal and any outstanding accrued and unpaid interest to the Issuer at that time. If in the event the Bonds are not repurchased on April 1, 2021, the Bonds shall be subject to the interest rate and redemption provisions set forth in the associated covenant agreement.&nbsp; Subsequent to December 31, 2020 the Company was informed that the&nbsp;bank will recall the loan and require the Company to repay the outstanding principal and any outstanding accrued and unpaid interest on April 1, 2021.&nbsp; As of December 31, 2020, the Company reclassified the entire Loan from long-term debt to current liability.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">The remaining principal payments required under the agreement for years ended December 31, and the current and long-term portion of the principal, are as follows:</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">In connection with the agreement, the Company incurred debt issuance costs of approximately $139,000 during 2016, which were deferred and are being amortized over the term of the Financing Agreement. Amortization of debt issuance costs was approximately $11,000 for 2020&nbsp;and 2019&nbsp;and is included in interest expense. Debt issuance costs of $85,000 are netted against long-term debt and current portion of long-term debt, respectively as of December 31, 2020 and 2019. The entire $85,000 of unamortized&nbsp;debt costs will be expensed when the loan is repaid in 2021.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><b>Paycheck Protection Program Loan</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">On April 18, 2020, Company entered into a loan pursuant to the Paycheck Protection Program under the CARES Act, as administered by the U.S. Small Business Administration (the &#8220;SBA&#8221;). The loan, in the principal amount of $1,214,500 (the &#8220;PPP Loan&#8221;), was disbursed by BMO Harris Bank National Association (&#8220;Lender&#8221;) on April 22, 2020, pursuant to a Paycheck Protection Program Promissory Note and Agreement (the &#8220;Note and Agreement&#8221;).</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">Under the CARES Act, loan forgiveness is available for the sum of documented payroll costs, covered rent payments, and covered utilities during an eight or twenty four-week period beginning on the approval date of the PPP Loan. For purposes of the CARES Act, payroll costs exclude compensation of an individual employee earning more than $100,000, prorated annually. Not more than 40% of the forgiven amount may be for non-payroll costs. Forgiveness is reduced if full-time headcount declines, or if salaries and wages for employees with salaries of $100,000 or less annually are reduced by more than 25%.&nbsp; During the fourth quarter of 2020, the Company submitted an application for 100% forgiveness of the&nbsp;PPP Loan.&nbsp; Prior to end of 2020, both the lender and the SBA forgave 100% of the Company's PPP loan.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">The Company accounts for the PPP Loan as debt in accordance with Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) 470, Debt and accrues interest in accordance with the interest method under FASB ASC 835-30.&nbsp; When the loan was forgiven,&nbsp;&nbsp;the Company reduced the liability by the amount forgiven and recorded a gain on extinguishment in the statement of operations.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;"><b>Line of Credit</b></p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">The Company also&nbsp;has a bank line of credit providing for borrowings of up to $2,050,000 which expires on August 30, 2021 and bears interest at 1.8 percentage points over the 30-day LIBOR rate.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company did not utilize this line of credit during 2020&nbsp;or 2019&nbsp;and there were no borrowings outstanding as of December 31, 2020&nbsp;or 2019.&nbsp;&nbsp;There are no financial covenants related to the line of credit, and the Company expects&nbsp;that it will secure a&nbsp;similar line of credit when the current line of credit expires.&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">Both the&nbsp; Duluth Development Authority Loan and the line of credit are collateralized by substantially all assets of the Company.</p>
</div>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 27pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;</p>

<div contenteditable="false" docsect="9" id="161322" sectdesc="Note to Financial Statements">&nbsp;</div>

<div data-td-parse-id="1" data-td-statement-type="note" data-td-v2v-id="1582756652620">
<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;">

		<tr style="vertical-align: top;">
			<td style="width: 27pt;">
			<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">8.</p>
			</td>
			<td>
			<p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER TRANSITION</p>
			</td>
		</tr>

</table>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:28.8pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:-28.8pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt 25pt; text-align: left;">On January 7, 2020, Mr. Ulland formally announced his retirement as President and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, effective February 10, 2020. Mr. Ulland will continue to serve as Chairman of the Board.&nbsp; On January 7, 2020, the Company also&nbsp;announced that Glenn Sandgren has been appointed to the position of Chief Executive Officer effective February 10, 2020. Mr. Sandgren has also been appointed to the Board of Directors of the Company, also effective February 10, 2020.&nbsp; The Company incurred one-time costs of approximately $365,000 in 2020 related to the Chief Executive officer transition including severance payments, signing bonus, relocation expenses and executive search consulting expenses.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:36pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><u>Item 9. Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure</u></b></p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">None.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><u>Item 9A. Controls and Procedures</u></b>&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><i>Disclosure Controls and Procedures</i></b><i>. &nbsp;</i>As of December&nbsp;31, 2020, an evaluation was carried out under the supervision and with the participation of our management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, of the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rule&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;)). Based upon that evaluation, the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer concluded that the design and operation of these disclosure controls and procedures were effective to ensure that information required to be disclosed by us in the reports that we file or submit under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in applicable rules&nbsp;and forms.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><i>Management&#8217;s Annual Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting. </i></b>Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(f)&nbsp;and 15d-15(f ) under the Exchange Act. Our internal control system is designed to provide reasonable assurance to our management and board of directors regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. Our internal control over financial reporting includes those policies and procedures that:</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">

		<tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
			<td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</td>
			<td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#8226;</p>
			</td>
			<td style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the Company;</p>
			</td>
		</tr>

</table>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:18pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">

		<tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
			<td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</td>
			<td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</td>
			<td style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Provide reasonable assurance that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the Company are being made only in accordance with authorizations of management and directors of the Company; and</p>
			</td>
		</tr>

</table>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:18pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">

		<tr style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
			<td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&nbsp;</td>
			<td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#8226;</td>
			<td style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
			<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Provide reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection of unauthorized acquisition, use or disposition of the Company&#8217;s assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.</p>
			</td>
		</tr>

</table>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:36pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:left;text-indent:-18pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">Management assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2020. In making this assessment, management used the 2013 criteria set forth by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO)&nbsp;in <i>Internal Control &#8212; Integrated Framework</i>. Based on management&#8217;s assessment and those criteria, management believes that, as of December&nbsp;31, 2020, the Company maintained effective internal control over financial reporting.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">This annual report does not include an attestation report of the Company&#8217;s registered public accounting firm regarding internal control over financial reporting. Our management&#8217;s report of the effectiveness on the design and operation of our internal control over financial reporting was not subject to attestation by the Company&#8217;s registered public accounting firm pursuant to rules&nbsp;of the Securities and Exchange Commission that permit the Company to provide only management&#8217;s report in this annual report.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><i>Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting.&nbsp;&nbsp;</i></b>As of the end of the period covered by this report, the Company conducted an evaluation, under the supervision and with the participation of the principal executive officer and principal financial officer, of the Company&#8217;s disclosure control and procedures (as defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;and 15d-15(e)&nbsp;under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the &#8220;Exchange Act&#8221;)).&nbsp; Based on this evaluation, the principal executive officer and principal financial officer concluded that the Company&#8217;s disclosure controls and procedures are effective to ensure that information required to be disclosed by the Company in reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act is (i)&nbsp;recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in SEC rules&nbsp;and forms and (ii)&nbsp;accumulated and communicated to the Company&#8217;s management, including its principal executive officer and principal financial officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt -2pt; text-align: left;">There was no change in the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting identified in connection with the evaluation required by Rule&nbsp;13a-15(d)&nbsp;and Rule&nbsp;15d-15(d)&nbsp;of the Exchange Act that occurred during the period covered by this report and that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting.</p>

<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt 7.2pt 0pt -2pt; text-align: left;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
